en.statement: Tailwind generates CSS for the utility classes it finds in your project when you compile your CSS.
en.explanation: Tailwind isn't one big prebuilt stylesheet: it builds just the styles your classes need at compile time, which is how a one-off class like bg-[#316ff6] works.

en.statement: Tailwind duplicates the p-4 CSS rule when two elements use p-4.
en.explanation: Tailwind reuses utility rules across elements.

en.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 retains compatibility with the leading ! utility modifier.
en.explanation: Tailwind still accepts the older modifier syntax, which is deprecated.

en.statement: Tailwind composes blur-sm and grayscale through separate CSS variables.
en.explanation: Tailwind's filter variables combine blur and grayscale.

en.statement: Tailwind requires shared utility styles to move into a custom CSS class.
en.explanation: Tailwind documents sharing utility markup through components or template partials.

en.statement: A hover utility can read a CSS variable supplied through an inline style.
en.explanation: The documented pattern uses hover:bg-(--bg-color-hover).

en.statement: For equally specific, equally important active utilities, later class-attribute order decides the winner.
en.explanation: For comparable utilities, Tailwind's stylesheet rule order resolves conflicts.

en.statement: In Tailwind CSS v4, bg-red-500! marks its generated declaration !important.
en.explanation: Tailwind adds !important to that utility's declarations.

en.statement: The important import option raises Tailwind utility selector specificity.
en.explanation: The import flag marks the entire utility output !important.

en.statement: With prefix(tw), Tailwind emits color variables such as --tw-color-red-500.
en.explanation: The prefix also applies to generated theme variable names.

en.statement: With prefix(tw), Tailwind CSS v4 accepts hover:tw:bg-red-500 as the prefixed hover class.
en.explanation: Tailwind places the prefix first: tw:hover:bg-red-500.

en.statement: A :root color variable can register matching Tailwind utilities.
en.explanation: Utility registration needs @theme, rather than :root.

en.statement: A --font-editor theme token can generate a font-weight utility.
en.explanation: Tailwind's --font-* namespace generates font-family utilities.

en.statement: Adding --font-script in @theme replaces the default font-family utilities.
en.explanation: New theme tokens extend the imported defaults.

en.statement: Redefining --color-red-500 in @theme changes the value used by bg-red-500.
en.explanation: Tailwind's bg-red-500 reads the redefined --color-red-500 token.

en.statement: In @theme, --color-*: initial removes default palette utilities.
en.explanation: Tailwind's color wildcard reset clears the imported palette API.

en.statement: In @theme, --*: initial removes Tailwind's flex utility.
en.explanation: Static utilities like flex survive theme resets.

en.statement: With @theme inline, --font-sans: var(--font-inter) makes font-sans reference var(--font-sans).
en.explanation: Tailwind emits font-family: var(--font-inter) for that utility.

en.statement: Tailwind emits unused theme variables when @theme static defines them.
en.explanation: Tailwind's static option retains unused theme variables in output.

en.statement: A CSS @import can share @theme tokens between Tailwind projects.
en.explanation: Importing the shared stylesheet supplies its theme definitions.

en.statement: Tailwind finds utility candidates by parsing the class attributes in your HTML templates.
en.explanation: Tailwind treats every source file as plain text and picks out class-like tokens wherever they appear, without parsing the file as code.

en.statement: Tailwind detects complete class strings selected from a lookup object.
en.explanation: Complete strings remain visible in scanned source.

en.statement: Tailwind automatically scans node_modules for utility classes.
en.explanation: Dependency files need explicit source registration.

en.statement: Tailwind excludes CSS files from automatic class detection.
en.explanation: Tailwind skips CSS sources.

en.statement: Tailwind resolves @source paths relative to the build's working directory.
en.explanation: Tailwind resolves @source paths from the stylesheet.

en.statement: With source(none), Tailwind scans paths registered through @source.
en.explanation: Explicit paths supply sources when automatic detection is disabled.

en.statement: An @source inline('underline') directive can generate an otherwise undetected utility.
en.explanation: Tailwind generates valid candidates supplied through @source inline().

en.statement: An @source inline('underline') directive can also generate hover:underline.
en.explanation: Variant classes need explicit inline-source entries.

en.statement: Tailwind expands bg-red-{100..900..100} inside @source inline() into candidate classes.
en.explanation: Brace ranges supply multiple candidates.

en.statement: In Tailwind CSS v4, hover: includes a media condition for primary-input hover capability.
en.explanation: Tailwind wraps the :hover rule in (hover: hover).

en.statement: A focus-within: utility can style a wrapper while its descendant has focus.
en.explanation: Tailwind's focus-within: rules match focus in the element or its descendants.

en.statement: Tailwind's disabled: variant matches a button that signals its state with aria-disabled="true" alone.
en.explanation: disabled: compiles to :disabled, which needs the native disabled state; a button marked only with aria-disabled="true" needs Tailwind's aria-disabled: variant.

en.statement: Tailwind's invalid: styles show on an empty required field before the user has typed anything.
en.explanation: invalid: compiles to :invalid, which matches as soon as the value fails validation; Tailwind's user-invalid: variant waits until the user has interacted with the field.

en.statement: Tailwind's checked: variant matches a checkbox through its checked HTML attribute.
en.explanation: Tailwind generates a :checked condition for live state.

en.statement: Tailwind's focus:invalid: utilities apply when both form-state conditions match.
en.explanation: Tailwind's focus:invalid: rules combine :focus and :invalid.

en.statement: With dark overridden to &:where(.dark, .dark *), Tailwind still requires the system's dark preference.
en.explanation: With the .dark selector override, Tailwind activates dark: through matching markup.

en.statement: With dark set to &:where([data-theme=dark], [data-theme=dark] *), dark: also targets the marked element.
en.explanation: The documented data-theme dark selector includes the marked element itself.

en.statement: Tailwind's selector-based dark variant can persist the user's theme choice in localStorage.
en.explanation: The application owns persistence of theme preferences.

en.statement: Tailwind's group-focus: responds to focus on an ancestor marked group.
en.explanation: Tailwind targets .group:focus ancestors.

en.statement: Tailwind's peer-invalid: can style a sibling that appears before the peer marker.
en.explanation: Tailwind's peer variants target following siblings.

en.statement: Tailwind's has-checked: can style an element containing a checked descendant.
en.explanation: Tailwind generates a :has(:checked) condition.

en.statement: Tailwind's group-has-[a]: looks for a link inside the styled element's own subtree.
en.explanation: group-has-[a]: runs its :has() check on the element marked group, so the link can sit anywhere inside that group.

en.statement: Tailwind's in-focus: variant reacts to focus on any parent element, whether or not that parent has the group class.
en.explanation: The in-* variants respond to a state change in any ancestor and need no marker class, so in-focus: also fires when an outer wrapper higher up receives focus.

en.statement: Tailwind's group-[.is-ready]: searches above the group marker for an .is-ready ancestor.
en.explanation: group-[.is-ready]: combines .group and .is-ready on one element.

en.statement: Tailwind's data-active: waits for data-active to equal 'true'.
en.explanation: Tailwind's data-active: tests attribute presence.

en.statement: Tailwind's aria-expanded: activates when aria-expanded='false'.
en.explanation: Tailwind matches aria-expanded="true" for aria-expanded:.

en.statement: Tailwind's sm: utilities target viewports below the sm threshold.
en.explanation: Tailwind generates a minimum-width condition for sm:.

en.statement: Tailwind excludes the md boundary from max-md: rules.
en.explanation: Tailwind's max-md: uses a strict upper comparison.

en.statement: Tailwind treats md:xl:flex as the bounded range form of its responsive API.
en.explanation: Tailwind uses md:max-xl: for a bounded viewport interval.

en.statement: Tailwind emits default lg: media queries that read --breakpoint-lg through var().
en.explanation: Tailwind embeds breakpoint lengths directly into media-query conditions.

en.statement: Setting --breakpoint-2xl: initial in @theme keeps 2xl: available at its original threshold.
en.explanation: Tailwind removes 2xl: when --breakpoint-2xl is set to initial.

en.statement: Above lg, equally specific normal md:w-32 and lg:w-48 utilities resolve to lg:w-48 in Tailwind's output.
en.explanation: Tailwind orders responsive rules by breakpoint size.

en.statement: Tailwind normalizes mixed px and rem breakpoint tokens before ordering responsive utility rules.
en.explanation: Mixed breakpoint units can produce unexpected generated ordering.

en.statement: Tailwind's min-[37rem]: produces a viewport threshold outside the named breakpoint scale.
en.explanation: Arbitrary variants supply one-off viewport thresholds.

en.statement: An @theme --breakpoint-tablet token automatically makes max-tablet: available.
en.explanation: Tailwind generates a maximum variant for a breakpoint.

en.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 routes container variants through a separately installed container-query plugin.
en.explanation: Container variants belong to Tailwind CSS v4's core.

en.statement: Tailwind CSS v4.3 uses @container-size for descendant utilities with block-size container units.
en.explanation: Tailwind's @container-size marker establishes size containment.

en.statement: Tailwind evaluates @md:flex using the viewport's width.
en.explanation: Tailwind's @md: variant checks an ancestor container's width.

en.statement: Tailwind's @sm: variant stops matching once its container reaches the @md size.
en.explanation: Tailwind compiles @sm: to @container (width >= 24rem), a minimum with no upper bound, so its styles stay active as the container grows past @md.

en.statement: Tailwind's @max-md: threshold tracks changes to --breakpoint-md in @theme.
en.explanation: Tailwind's @max-md: threshold belongs to the --container-* scale.

en.statement: Tailwind compiles @sm:@max-md: into a bounded container-query interval.
en.explanation: Tailwind's @sm:@max-md: stack supplies lower and upper thresholds.

en.statement: Tailwind's @sm/main: selects @container/main beyond a nearer, differently named container.
en.explanation: Tailwind's named container variant identifies its intended ancestor.

en.statement: A --container-card token in @theme makes Tailwind's max-w-card utility available.
en.explanation: Tailwind's --container-* namespace also registers size utilities.

en.statement: Tailwind accepts container units as arbitrary utility values, such as w-[50cqw].
en.explanation: Tailwind's width declaration retains the supplied cqw value.

en.statement: Tailwind inlines a variable's resolved value when compiling w-(--panel-width).
en.explanation: Tailwind emits width: var(--panel-width) for w-(--panel-width).

en.statement: Tailwind can compile text-(length:--label-size) as color when --label-size contains a color.
en.explanation: The length: hint selects Tailwind's font-size API.

en.statement: Tailwind decodes underscores in grid-cols-[1fr_2fr] into spaces in the generated value.
en.explanation: Tailwind emits grid-template-columns: 1fr 2fr.

en.statement: Tailwind decodes the underscore in bg-[url('/team_photo.png')] into a space in its generated URL.
en.explanation: Tailwind preserves underscores inside URL values.

en.statement: Tailwind preserves the escaped underscore in before:content-['user\_name'] in the generated content.
en.explanation: Tailwind keeps an escaped underscore literal in arbitrary values.

en.statement: Tailwind emits an ordinary CSS custom property from md:[--panel-gap:24px].
en.explanation: Tailwind's [--panel-gap:24px] generates a CSS variable assignment.

en.statement: Tailwind substitutes the element carrying a class for & in the arbitrary variant [&.selected]:underline.
en.explanation: Tailwind's & placeholder identifies the utility's own element.

en.statement: Tailwind accepts [@supports(display:grid)]:grid with an implicit utility target.
en.explanation: Arbitrary at-rule variants work with the & placeholder omitted.

en.statement: In Tailwind CSS v4, first:*:pt-0 styles the first child inside the element carrying the class.
en.explanation: Tailwind applies first: before *:, targeting children of an element that is itself a first child.

en.statement: Importing tailwindcss includes Preflight in Tailwind's base layer.
en.explanation: The default Tailwind import brings in preflight.css under layer(base).

en.statement: Preflight retains a paragraph's browser-provided vertical margins in Tailwind's base styles.
en.explanation: Preflight resets paragraph margins to zero.

en.statement: Preflight's border reset strips the browser-drawn borders from text inputs and buttons.
en.explanation: Preflight applies border: 0 solid to every element plus ::before, ::after, ::backdrop and ::file-selector-button, which overrides the user-agent borders on text inputs and buttons.

en.statement: Preflight selects Tailwind's text-2xl token as the default font size for h1 headings.
en.explanation: Preflight makes h1 font size and font weight inherit.

en.statement: Preflight preserves browser numbering on ordered lists in Tailwind's base styles.
en.explanation: Preflight applies list-style: none to ordered lists.

en.statement: Preflight changes images and videos to block display in Tailwind's base styles.
en.explanation: Preflight includes img and video in its display: block reset.

en.statement: Preflight stretches a narrow image to its parent's width with a width: 100% declaration.
en.explanation: Preflight constrains images with max-width: 100% rather than assigning that width.

en.statement: Tailwind's docs put a project's own element defaults, such as h1 styles, in @layer base rather than @layer components.
en.explanation: Element defaults belong in Tailwind's base layer, for example @layer base { h1 { color: red; } }; the docs keep @layer components for class-based components like .card.

en.statement: In Tailwind CSS v4, a normal utility beats a conflicting normal @layer components rule with a more specific selector.
en.explanation: Tailwind orders its utilities layer after components; for declarations without !important a later cascade layer wins whatever the selector specificity.

en.statement: Preflight selects content-box as the default box-sizing value for its reset targets.
en.explanation: Preflight sets box-sizing: border-box on its reset targets.

en.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 uses property count as a sorting criterion for custom @utility rules.
en.explanation: Tailwind's sorting helps utilities with fewer properties override broader custom utilities.

en.statement: A custom @utility tab-4 definition lets Tailwind generate focus:tab-4.
en.explanation: Tailwind registers custom utilities with its existing variant API.

en.statement: Tailwind inserts @utility definitions into its components layer alongside component styles.
en.explanation: Tailwind inserts custom utilities into the utilities layer.

en.statement: A nested &::-webkit-scrollbar rule inside @utility styles the scrollbar of the element using that utility.
en.explanation: Nesting inside @utility adds an extra selector to the generated utility, as in the docs' scrollbar-hidden example.

en.statement: With @theme { --tab-size-team: 8; }, @utility tab-* { tab-size: --value(--tab-size-*); } gives tab-team tab-size: 8.
en.explanation: Tailwind resolves the team suffix against --tab-size-team.

en.statement: @utility tabstop-* { tab-size: --value(integer); } accepts tabstop-[8] as a matching utility.
en.explanation: Tailwind accepts tabstop-[8] when tabstop-* uses --value([integer]).

en.statement: Tailwind replaces an unresolved --value() declaration with the property's initial value.
en.explanation: Tailwind omits declarations whose --value() calls fail to resolve.

en.statement: For tab-2 with @theme { --tab-size-2: 8; }, Tailwind's --value(--tab-size-*, integer) picks the theme value.
en.explanation: Tailwind tries --value() arguments in order and uses the first successful match.

en.statement: Defining @utility shift-* also registers Tailwind's corresponding -shift-* classes.
en.explanation: Tailwind uses a separate @utility -shift-* definition for the negative form.

en.statement: Tailwind joins selectors when @apply reuses an existing utility inside a custom rule.
en.explanation: Tailwind inserts utility declarations into the rule containing @apply.

en.statement: Tailwind applies @variant dark to declarations nested inside a custom CSS rule.
en.explanation: The @variant block wraps those declarations in the chosen Tailwind condition.

en.statement: Tailwind uses @reference to expose main-stylesheet definitions inside separately processed CSS Modules.
en.explanation: @reference makes theme variables, custom utilities, and custom variants available to CSS Modules.

en.statement: In a customized project, @reference 'tailwindcss' exposes app.css custom utilities.
en.explanation: A customized project's separate stylesheets reference its main stylesheet to see its custom definitions.

en.statement: Tailwind copies referenced stylesheet rules into component output when it processes @reference.
en.explanation: @reference supplies definitions while omitting the referenced stylesheet's emitted styles.

en.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 starts its stylesheet through @import 'tailwindcss'.
en.explanation: Tailwind's current entry stylesheet imports the framework using CSS @import.

en.statement: Tailwind bundles local CSS @import files into the project's compiled stylesheet.
en.explanation: Tailwind performs CSS import bundling during compilation.

en.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 adds vendor prefixes itself, which makes autoprefixer unnecessary in its PostCSS setup.
en.explanation: Vendor prefixing is part of Tailwind's own CSS processing in v4, so the upgrade guide removes autoprefixer from the PostCSS plugin list.

en.statement: Tailwind's docs name the PostCSS plugin as the most seamless way to add Tailwind to SvelteKit.
en.explanation: Tailwind's docs call the Vite plugin the most seamless way to integrate with frameworks like Laravel, SvelteKit, React Router, Nuxt and SolidJS.

en.statement: Tailwind CLI provides a standalone executable that performs Tailwind compilation outside Node.js.
en.explanation: The standalone Tailwind CLI executable runs independently of a Node.js installation.

en.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 documents Sass as a supported preprocessing stage in its build workflow.
en.explanation: Tailwind CSS v4's documented workflow is not designed for Sass, Less, or Stylus.

en.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 automatically discovers tailwind.config.js during compilation.
en.explanation: Tailwind CSS v4 loads a JavaScript configuration when CSS explicitly names it with @config.

en.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 gives CSS definitions precedence when legacy configuration values conflict.
en.explanation: Tailwind merges CSS and legacy configuration where possible; conflicting CSS definitions take precedence.

en.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 honors corePlugins, safelist, and separator in a JavaScript configuration.
en.explanation: Tailwind CSS v4 excludes corePlugins, safelist, and separator from supported JavaScript options.

en.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 retains theme() as a deprecated compatibility function.
en.explanation: Tailwind's theme() function remains available for legacy usage despite its deprecated status.

en.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 exposes resolveConfig for resolving a legacy JavaScript theme.
en.explanation: Tailwind CSS v4 removes the resolveConfig function exported by v3.

en.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 preserves an untouched to-* stop when a dark:from-* utility changes a gradient.
en.explanation: Changing a gradient stop through a v4 variant retains the other stop values.

en.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 uses currentColor as the default color for borders and rings.
en.explanation: Tailwind CSS v4's default border and ring colors follow currentColor.

en.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 resets scale-150 when focus:transform-none becomes active.
en.explanation: Tailwind CSS v4 uses an individual scale property; focus:scale-none resets scale-150.

en.statement: Tailwind CSS v4's space-y-* selector filters out children carrying a hidden attribute.
en.explanation: Tailwind's v4 space-y-* selector matches direct children except the last, including hidden children.

en.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 puts divide-y-* separators on the bottom edge of preceding children.
en.explanation: Tailwind's v4 divide-y-* utilities assign bottom borders to direct children except the last.

en.statement: In Tailwind CSS v4, --container-* tokens in @theme set the container utility's centering and padding.
en.explanation: The upgrade guide replaces v3's container center and padding options with CSS: @utility container { margin-inline: auto; padding-inline: 2rem; }.
